name: measuring-scale
title: Measuring scale
tagline: Graduated instrument read against an indicator — ruler, capacity jug or dial scale; ticks and the reading derived, occlude to "?" for reading off.
description: A graduated measuring instrument read against an indicator, in one of three forms chosen by kind: a horizontal ruler (cm/mm ticks with an object lying along the scale — the reading is the object’s length, so an object that does not start at zero gives the read-the-difference case), a vertical capacity jug (litre/millilitre ticks with a blue fill level), or a rotary dial weighing scale (a needle on a 0–max face). The author writes the scale (min, max, the numbered-tick interval and any subdivisions, and the unit) and the true measurement (an object’s span on a ruler, or a value on a jug/dial); the tick positions and numbers, the indicator’s position, the reading, the bracketing “between two ticks” values and a ruler’s endpoint readings are all derived. Tick numbers thin and minor ticks drop out when the scale gets dense, so the marks never collide. The reading occludes to “?” for a question (the indicator stays visible to be read), highlights amber for the answer, and is echoed by an optional fill-in stem sentence (“The pencil is 8 cm long”) and a free caption.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever a lesson reads a measuring instrument: measuring length with a ruler (including the read-the-difference case where the object starts part-way along, not at 0), reading a measuring jug or cylinder for capacity, and reading a kitchen/dial scale for mass. Pick kind: "ruler" for length, "jug" for capacity, "dial" for mass (any unit string works — cm, mm, ml, l, g, kg). Author the scale and the true measurement; never write the reading. Common configurations — read the scale (a question): reading.occlude true hides the number while the object/fill/needle stays visible ("how long / how much / how heavy?"); add reading.highlight to amber the answer once revealed. Read the difference (the key ruler case): give object.from a non-zero start and show.endValues true so both ends are read, then the length to − from is the derived answer — occlude it for the question. Between two ticks: reading.interval true adds "between {lo} and {hi}" using the numbered ticks bracketing the reading (for a partial-unit needle or fill level). Stem sentence: stem { noun, measure } renders Oak’s fill-in twin "The {noun} is {reading} {unit} {measure}" (measure = long / tall / full / heavy…), with the value occlusion-aware. Cross-block conventions: keep the same scale (min/max/major/minor/unit) across the blocks of one lesson so pupils read a steady instrument; choose a major interval that leaves the numbered ticks legible (the model thins labels if you overshoot, but a sensible major reads best); use minor for the subdivisions a real instrument shows (10 for cm→mm, 5 for 100→every-20). Staged builds: open on the object/fill/needle with the reading occluded, then over stages show the endpoints (ruler), reveal the reading, and highlight it — the base state (a labelled scale with the indicator) stands alone as a sensible figure. Synonyms teachers use: measuring scale, reading scales, ruler, measuring jug, measuring cylinder, weighing scale, dial, gauge, length, capacity, volume, mass, weight, graduations, divisions, read the difference, between the marks.

kind.description: Which instrument to draw. "ruler": a horizontal cm/mm scale with an object lying along it (reading = the object’s length). "jug": a vertical capacity container with a blue fill level (reading = the fill value). "dial": a rotary weighing scale with a needle on a 0–max face (reading = the needle value). Use "object" with a ruler and "value" with a jug or dial.

scale.description: The graduated scale: where the numbered ticks fall and what they measure. The same shape for all three kinds (a ruler’s scale runs left→right, a jug’s bottom→top, a dial’s clockwise from the top).

min.description: Value at the start of the scale (the left end / the bottom / the top of the dial). Default 0 — almost always 0 for a primary instrument.

max.description: Value at the end of the scale (the right end / the top / back to the top of the dial, one full turn). Must be greater than min.

major.description: Interval between NUMBERED (major) ticks, e.g. 1 for a cm ruler, 100 for a 0–500 ml jug, 100 for a 0–1000 g dial. Numbered ticks fall at min, min+major, … up to max.

minor.description: Number of equal SUBDIVISIONS between consecutive numbered ticks — the small unnumbered marks (a real instrument’s fine graduations). 10 turns a cm ruler’s gaps into mm; 5 turns a 100-unit gap into 20s. 0 = no minor ticks. Minor ticks drop out automatically if they would be too close to read.

unit.description: Unit symbol shown on the scale and in the reading, e.g. "cm", "mm", "ml", "l", "g", "kg". Free text — the model does not convert units.

object.description: RULER ONLY: the thing lying along the ruler. The reading is its LENGTH (to − from), computed — so an object whose from is not 0 gives the read-the-difference case automatically. Ignored for jug/dial.

from.description: Scale value at the LEFT end of the object. Default 0 (aligned to the start of the ruler, the simple case). Set a non-zero from for the read-the-difference / non-zero-start case.

to.description: Scale value at the RIGHT end of the object. Must be greater than from. The reading is to − from.

label.description: Name of the object drawn on it (e.g. "pencil", "ribbon", "leaf"). Used in the stem sentence too if stem.noun is omitted.

fill.description: Categorical colour of the object — a primary manipulative reads warmer in colour. Default "teal". (Blue here is the categorical blue; the amber result colour is reserved for highlight.)

value.description: JUG/DIAL ONLY: the true reading — the jug’s fill level or the dial’s needle value, in scale units. The fill height / needle angle is computed from it. Ignored for a ruler (which uses object).

reading.description: How the derived reading (the answer) is presented. The reading itself is always computed — this object only controls its display.

show.description: Show the reading readout (the number + unit) beside/below the figure. Default true. false hides the readout entirely — use when only the stem sentence should carry the value.

occlude.description: Render every derived value as "?" — the readout, the stem-sentence value and the between-phrase — so the figure poses "read the scale". The object/fill/needle stays visible (it is what the pupil reads). Endpoint readings are controlled separately by show.endValues. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber the reading — answer emphasis once revealed. Default false. Reserve for the result, not for default display.

interval.description: Also state "between {lo} and {hi}" using the numbered ticks bracketing the reading — the partial-unit phrasing for a needle/level that sits between two marks. Omitted automatically when the reading lands exactly on a numbered tick. Default false.

places.description: Decimal places for the displayed reading. Default: just enough to show the value exactly (no trailing zeros). Set e.g. 1 to force "2.0 l".

stem.description: Optional fill-in STEM SENTENCE — the verbal twin of the figure (Oak’s "The __ is __ cm long"). Rendered in a warm caption band; the value is occlusion-aware (shows "?" when reading.occlude).

noun.description: The subject of the sentence, e.g. "pencil", "water", "apple". Falls back to object.label, else "reading". The sentence reads "The {noun} is {reading} {unit} {measure}".

measure.description: The trailing descriptor, e.g. "long" (length), "tall"/"full" (capacity), "heavy" (mass). Omit for none — "The water is 350 ml".

caption.description: Optional line in a warm band below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Distinct from the auto stem sentence. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

endValues.description: RULER: show the scale reading at each END of the object (e.g. 3 and 11) — the scaffold for the read-the-difference case. Default false (the simple case shows just the length).

minorTicks.description: Draw the minor (subdivision) ticks set by scale.minor. Default true. false keeps only the numbered ticks.

tickLabels.description: Number the major ticks. Default true. false gives a bare graduated scale (the marks without numbers) — a harder read.

examples.label: Worked ruler — a crayon 0–8 cm with the stem sentence
Hard case — read the difference: a ribbon from 3 to 11 cm (length occluded)
Worked jug — 350 ml between the 300 and 400 marks
Occluded question — dial scale: what is the mass of the apple?
Worked dial — a partial-unit reading of 250 g, answer highlighted
Blank answer space — how long is the pencil? (length occluded)
